prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on what you need (avatar vs. stock footage, short social clip vs. 30–60s brand spot, budget, languages, API access, etc.). Below are the top options by use case plus quick pros/cons so you can pick the best match.

If you want a single recommendation for a polished, avatar-led ad: Synthesia is the safest pick for corporate-quality AI presenters and multi‑language voiceovers. But read the details below and tell me your exact needs if you want a tailored pick.

Top choices (what they’re best at)

- Synthesia
  - Best for: Professional, presenter-style ads using realistic AI avatars.
  - Strengths: High-quality avatars, many languages, brand controls, script → video workflow.
  - Weaknesses: Costlier than simple template tools; limited free tier.

- HeyGen (formerly Movio / similar providers)
  - Best for: Cheaper avatar-based videos with fast turnaround.
  - Strengths: Good quality, simpler pricing; useful for many short ads.
  - Weaknesses: Slightly less realism/advanced controls than top-tier players.

- Pictory
  - Best for: Turning blog posts/long videos into short ad clips automatically.
  - Strengths: Automatic summarization, easy repurposing, subtitle and format options.
  - Weaknesses: Less control over highly stylized creative edits.

- OpusClip / Wisecut
  - Best for: Auto-creating short social ads from long-form videos (TikTok/Reels/Shorts).
  - Strengths: Auto-highlights, captioning, aspect-ratio exports optimized for social.
  - Weaknesses: Not for full bespoke brand spots.

- Lumen5 / InVideo / Canva (video)
  - Best for: Template-based ad creation and quick storyboarding from script.
  - Strengths: Large template libraries, stock assets, easy drag-and-drop, low learning curve.
  - Weaknesses: Less “AI presenter” capability; final result can feel templated.

- Runway (Gen/Creative suite)
  - Best for: Advanced generative video editing and creative effects.
  - Strengths: Powerful generative tools, frame-level editing, unique visuals.
  - Weaknesses: More of a creative toolset — steeper learning curve, may be overkill for simple ads.

- Movio / Elai.ai / Rephrase.ai
  - Best for: Variants on avatar-based and text→video solutions. Good when you want different voices/avatars across campaigns.
  - Strengths/weaknesses vary; generally flexible for scalable ad campaigns.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Output type: avatar, stock footage + text, or repurposed clips?
- Platform targets: social short-form vs. broadcast/YouTube.
- Languages & voices: Do you need many locales or custom voice cloning?
- Brand control: custom backgrounds, logos, brand voice?
- Budget: pay-as-you-go vs. subscription vs. enterprise licensing.
- Rights & compliance: commercial license, voice/likeness consent if cloning.

Other tips
- Always test with a short campaign / free trial before buying a big plan.
- Check commercial use and voice/face licensing and IP clauses.
- For best performance, A/B test multiple versions (different hooks, thumbnails, CTA).
- If you have existing long-form content, try repurposing tools first — fastest ROI.

If you tell me: (1) ad length, (2) style (live presenter, animation, stock footage), (3) platform (TikTok/IG/Reels, YouTube, FB, connected TV), and (4) budget, I’ll recommend the single best tool and a workflow for you.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
